definition: Family support services are voluntary, free services for expectant parents and families with very young children that provide practical guidance and support to improve caregiving and family psychosocial well-being. They can include counselling, parenting classes, and home visiting support, especially for families facing greater psychosocial strain.

reasons: The packet supports that the program offers free-of-charge and voluntary services, and that it targets expectant parents and families with children aged 0–3 years; however, it does not explicitly state that these services are “for expectant parents and families with very young children” in the same wording as the definition (it specifies “expectant parents and families with a child aged 0–3 years”).

The packet supports that services include “pregnancy or child guidance counseling,” parenting classes, and home visiting programs, but it does not explicitly support the definition’s framing that they “provide practical guidance and support to improve caregiving” (it discusses improving psychosocial care for families and supporting caregivers’ ability in general terms, but not this caregiving-improvement mechanism as stated).

The definition states services improve “family psychosocial well-being”; while the packet describes a “special focus on families experiencing heightened psychosocial burden” and aims at improving “psychosocial care,” it does not clearly substantiate the specific wording “psychosocial well-being.”

“Especially for families facing greater psychosocial strain” is directionally supported by the packet’s “special focus on families experiencing heightened psychosocial burden,” but the exact “greater psychosocial strain” phrasing is not directly supported as such.
